text: In a village called Shri Rambburur, many beggars  used to sit outside the railway station. One of them was a boy named Serju. Sergu had a younger  sister named Rama. Rama was a very calm and intelligent girl. She studied in the fifth class.  Since their parents had passed away when Serju was only 15 years old, the responsibility of  taking care of Rama fell on him. Their financial condition was extremely poor. Poverty never  seemed to leave them. To pay for his sister's studies and to feed both of them, Sergu used  to beg outside the railway station. Please give something in God's name. God will bless you. Yeah,  take this. Who knows where all these people come from. After saying this, the man leaves. Sanju  again starts begging. Please help in God's name. God will fulfill all your wishes. Son, instead of  begging here, you should work somewhere. God has given you two hands and two legs. After saying  this, the old man leaves. Hearing those words, Sergu feels deeply hurt. He makes a promise  to himself. I could not complete my education, but I will educate my sister well and help  her stand on her own feet. Thinking this, Sergu again starts begging. Suddenly his eyes  fall on a tea stall nearby. Many people are working there. A thought comes to his mind. What  if I go there and ask for work? Maybe I can get a job. Let me try once. Sergu goes to the tea stall  and says to the owner, "Sir, can I get some work here? Aren't you the same beggar boy? Why do you  suddenly want a job?" "Sir, I barely need work. I don't want to live the life of a beggar anymore.  I want to do something through hard work. I will work sincerely. Please give me one chance. All  right. But you will have to do whatever work is given to you. Yes, sir. I will do whatever work  you asked me to do. Sirju happily returns home and tells [music] his sister, "Rama, I'm so happy  today. I finally got a job. I will never beg." Brother, this is wonderful news. Now you won't  have to spend your life as a [music] beggar. I am so happy. Now I will earn through hard  work and you focus only on your studies. The next day Sergu joins the tea stall [music]  and starts doing all the work sincerely. He works with great honesty and dedication. The tea  seller becomes very happy with [music] his hard work. One day the tea seller calls Sju and says,  [music] "Serg you work with so much dedication. Why don't you complete your unfinished education?  You can become very successful in life. Mark my words. The fact that you think so much about me  itself means a lot to me. Whatever I earn is spent on my sister's education and our daily expenses.  How can I afford my studies too? [music] You start

studying. I will pay for your education. When  you earn enough in the future, you can return the money to me. Okay. Hearing this, Sergu becomes  emotional and tears fill his eyes. Sir, after my parents only you supported me. I will never forget  this kindness in my life. All [music] right, now go back to work and in the evening get admission  in the night school. [music] Yes sir. That evening Sanju gets admission into a night school. [music]  For him it feels like a dream coming true. Now Sergio thinks that if he works even harder he  can earn more money [music] and also repay the tea sellers kindness faster. So every morning  he starts delivering newspapers. Then he works sincerely at the tea stall during [music] the day  and in whatever time remains he studies. Meanwhile both Serju and Rama are very intelligent.  Rama always stands first in her school. One day [music] Rama says to her brother,  "Brother, I was thinking if we keep some snacks and food items at Uncle's Tea stall, the  business will grow much more and [music] the income will increase too." That's very good idea,  Rama. I will talk to the owner. If he agrees, we will work very hard on it. Yes, brother.  I will help in whatever way I can. No Rama, you should focus only on your studies. I  will manage everything else. Okay, brother. Sergu goes to the tea cellar and shares [music]  his idea. Hey Sergu, you are late today. Sir, I had some work so I got delayed. Sir, I [music]  was thinking if we sell snacks along with tea, then customers will get everything in [music] one  place and our business will improve. Your idea is good. [music] You alone will have to manage all  this. I am too old for extra work now. Don't worry sir, I will [music] handle everything. Then fine,  I trust you completely. After that, [music] Sergu start selling snacks along with tea. Since  customers started getting everything at one place, more and more people [music] began coming  to the tea stall. Seeing the growing crowd, the tea seller becomes very [music] happy. Now he  fully trusts Sergu and believes that Sergu will take the business forward. Sergio studies at night  and works [music] during the day. Slowly his hard work starts showing results. The small tea stall  turns into a much bigger shop. Within a few years, Sergu repays all the [music] money for his  education to the tea seller. Sergu completes his studies and Rama also passes her 12th exams  with the highest marks in [music] the entire district. Sergu's hard work turns one small tea  into three successful shops. The business grows so much [music] that people specially come there for  tea and snacks. One day tea seller said to Serju,

"Sirju, with your hard work, you turned this tiny  tea [music] stall into a huge business. All this is the reward of your hard work, son. Sir, all  this happened [music] only because of you. If you had not helped a beggar like me and given  me a chance to work, I would never have reached here." [music] By giving you a chance, I changed  my own destiny too. Because of you, my small tea business [music] becomes so big. From today, one  of these shops belongs to you. You will manage it from now on. Sure, sir. As you say, I will take  full responsibility for the shop. With time, Sergu and Rama both become successful [music] in  life. Sergu, who was once a bagger, becomes the owner of a hotel, and Rama completes [music]  her studies and gets a job in a good company.
